implementation.integration: pure internal module; no production imports, HTTP mounts, repository, identity allocator, environment reads or external effects

semantics.companyAuthority: company_reference preserves the existing organizations.id as organizationId. It does not allocate or replace a company or attest durable existence.
semantics.enterpriseIdentity: enterprise_group_identity is a separate typed namespace; its ID is not an alias of organizations.id, a parent-owner record, or a tenant grant.
semantics.locationIdentity: location_identity is identified by its explicit organizationId and id together. The same UUID text in another company scope is a different typed identity.
semantics.legacyIdentity: legacy_location_reference preserves organizationId, the exact existing office/headquarters key and a pinned profile snapshot. It is never a canonical location allocation, mapping or automatic adoption.
semantics.association: Relationships declare explicit metadata references only. They confer no legal/common ownership, franchise participation, active membership, permission, reporting visibility or data transfer. This grammar selects no enterprise-owner or franchise policy.
semantics.provenance: declarationId, declaredByActorId, declaredAt are copied declaration metadata; identity validation does not verify the actor, issuer, source authenticity, currentness or authority.
semantics.immutability: All returned records, nested provenance/profile pins, graph arrays and graph are copied and frozen. This is in-process contract immutability, not a durable uniqueness/versioning or persistence guarantee.
semantics.literalIdentifiers: UUIDs are primitive canonical lower-case hyphenated text, without coercion, case-folding, trimming or UUID allocation. UUID syntax alone never proves database existence; even a nil value is only a literal ID and never a wildcard.
semantics.closedShapes: Only exact own enumerable data fields are accepted. Unknown/missing/null/undefined fields where a value is required, accessors, symbols, hidden fields, inherited records and unsupported kinds deny; no authority defaults.
semantics.determinism: Graph results sort identities by typed composite key and relationships by ID using deterministic string comparison. Input records/arrays are not mutated.

graphRules: An explicit contract marker and dense identities/relationships arrays are required; undefined does not become an empty graph.
An explicitly empty graph is valid reference data and adopts nothing.
Typed identity keys are unique within a batch, even for identical repeated declarations; conflicting declarations are not merged.
Location and legacy references require an explicitly declared matching company reference.
Each relationship endpoint must exist in the correct typed namespace; a same-ID company cannot satisfy a group or location reference.
Relationship IDs are unique across kinds; duplicate endpoint pairs also deny even with different IDs.
Every canonical location requires an explicit matching company_location_reference; identity scope does not silently create an edge.
Legacy references cannot satisfy canonical location edges and never produce one.
Distinct associations remain metadata and do not determine ownership/cardinality permissions. Group hierarchy, regions, franchises and access-grant relationship kinds are unsupported.

legacySnapshot.version: Exact org-profile-v positive decimal text up to 100 characters, not coerced through Number; large accepted historical version text is preserved.
legacySnapshot.key: Existing Business Profile stable-key syntax: [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}; case and punctuation preserved.
legacySnapshot.matching: Supplied company scope and all three pin fields must match exactly. The legacy key must exist exactly in the explicit source-key list.
legacySnapshot.ambiguity: Duplicate keys and case-ambiguous keys in the supplied snapshot deny rather than being folded into a new identity.
legacySnapshot.boundary: Matching validates equality/existence inside the supplied snapshot only. It does not query active Business Profile, verify freshness, authorize a session or certify an authentic source. Future authenticated consumers must resolve current trusted server authority separately.

batchBounds.meaning: Per-invocation resource bounds only; not plan, seat, company, location or commercial allowances.

persistence.reason: No durable repository is needed to define these pure contracts. No schema, data/backfill, membership migration or old-record reassignment occurs.
persistence.rollout: Additive module and tests with no existing runtime caller. No persistence upgrade or data conversion is required.
persistence.rollback: No schema or data rollback operation is introduced or exercised; normal release rollback disposition remains owned by root. Durable existence, transaction concurrency and live persistence are not claimed.

historical1ARelease.evidenceBoundary: Previously earned 1A release facts from the root source-linked ledger; not fresh 1B production/runtime proof.

validation.tier: direct actual pure-module tests; no mocked repository or copied validator
cases: explicit valid identities/relationships and empty graph
same-ID different-kind confusion and explicit typed separation
company-scoped location identity without bare-ID cross-company fallback
duplicate identities, relationship IDs, pairs and unknown/missing endpoints
missing/null/undefined required fields and extra authority/adoption keys
deep copied frozen output and deterministic JSON roundtrip
declaration provenance, counterfeit assurance fields and getters without invocation
exact legacy key/company/profile pin matching, ambiguous/unknown keys and large version text
dense bounded arrays without implicit product entitlements
